paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I'm not going to pretend it isn't. God tells Ezekiel to speak against the mountains of Israel, where the people had set up their idols and altars (Ezekiel 6:2-4). He says the people will fall there, and the reason is the idols they gave their hearts to. Through all of it He keeps saying one thing: "you will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 6:7)

Here's what I want you to hold onto. Idols never stay small. Those hills and green trees were where the people "offered fragrant incense to all their idols," and God calls what was in their hearts "adulterous" (Ezekiel 6:13, 6:9). Whatever we hand our hearts to besides Him, He sees it, and He is grieved by it. And look at what He says about His warning: "I did not declare in vain." (Ezekiel 6:10) When God speaks, He means it, and that is why He can be trusted.

But I'm telling you, don't leave without the little word in the middle: "Yet I will leave a remnant." (Ezekiel 6:8) Even inside this hard message, God keeps some of them, and they remember Him in a faraway land. I know a little about being far from home and wondering if anybody remembers you. God is the One who does the remembering, and He is the One who brings people back to Him. So ask yourself, baker: what is sitting on the high places of my life? Turn your face toward Him, because the One who warns you is the One who keeps a remnant.
